7031.t: From διδάσκω (dĭdắskō, “to teach”). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀇𐀅𐀏𐀩 (di-da-ka-re).

7048.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek διοικέω (dioikéō) Ancient Greek -τις (-tĭs) Ancient Greek -σις (-sĭs) Ancient Greek διοίκησις From διοικέω (dioikéō) + -σις (-sĭs), from δια- (dia-) + οἶκος (oîkos, “house”).

7049.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “across”) + οἰκοδομέω (oikodoméō, “to build a house”).

7085.t: Uncertain. Perhaps related to διδράσκω (didráskō, “to run”) and suffixed with -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix), though the origin of the sequence -πέ- (-pé-) is unclear.

7056.t: The origin is uncertain, possibly from Proto-Hellenic *dipʰtʰérā. Related to διψάρα (dipsára, “writing-tablet; piece of leather”) and Mycenaean Greek 𐀇𐁇𐀨 (di-pte-ra).

7066.t: From διαγιγνώσκω (dĭăgĭgnṓskō, “distinguish; discern”) + -σις (-sĭs), from δια- (dĭă-) + γιγνώσκω (gĭgnṓskō, “know”).

7023.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “in different directions, asunder”) + φορέω (phoréō, “to wear; to hold, possess, bear”).

7084.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dh₃tós (“given”). By surface analysis, the root of δίδωμι (dídōmi) + -τός (-tós).
